html:
On 22 May 1990 North Yemen and South Yemen merged to form the Republic of Yemen, with Sana'a as capital and the northern leader Ali Abdullah Saleh as president.

The south's Soviet patron was collapsing and both states had found oil near their border. The union was proclaimed in Aden. But the two armies were never merged, and southerners felt shut out. In 1994 southern leaders declared secession, and northern forces won a short civil war and took Aden.

Southern resentment lived on, in a separatist movement that grew in the 2000s. In the war since 2014 the south has been held by separatist forces again. See also the Aden Emergency.
sum: On 22 May 1990 North Yemen and South Yemen merged to form the Republic of Yemen, with Sana'a as capital and the northern leader Ali Abdullah Saleh as president.
